Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tapin Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of the Regional Government of Tapin Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tapin.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Tapin Regency.
5. Agency is the Agency for Women's Empowerment and Family Planning of Tapin Regency.
6. Head of Agency is the Head of the Agency for Women's Empowerment and Family Planning of Tapin Regency.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that have equality in accordance with the development and socio-cultural conditions of society.
8. Gender-Based Violence is any act of deviation caused by an imbalance in the relationship between women and men that results in misery or suffering of women including children, whether physically, sexually and/or psychologically, including threats, certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily that occurs in the private/domestic sphere and in the public sphere.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.
10. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capabilities so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.

ll.Disability is a permanent physical, mental and intellectual, or sensory impairment.

THE REGENT OF TAPIN,

Considering:
a. that women as a national asset who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination; b. that in addition to protection as referred to in letter a, women need to be empowered so that they can actualize their potential optimally to participate in development; c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letters a and b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Protection and Empowerment of Women; In view of: 1. Article 18 paragraph (6) of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia; 2. Article 13

(1) The Regent implements policies, programs and activities for the protection of women, to eliminate all forms of discrimination and violence against women in the region.

(2) The implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be coordinated by the Vice Regent.

(3) The work unit whose duties and functions handle the empowerment of women implements policies, programs and activities for the protection of women that have been established, and in its implementation cooperates with Regional Work Units, Community Institutions, Universities, and civil society.

(4) The implementation as referred to in paragraph (3) is in the form of: policy analysis, coordination, advocacy, socialization, communication, information, and education (KIE), training, service facilitation, service provision, model development, and other forms.

5. The integration of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women into regional development planning, which is set forth in planning and budget documents covering the Regional Long-Term Development Plan (RPJPD), Regional Medium-Term Plan (RPJMD), Regional Work Unit Strategic Plan (Renstra SKPD), Regional Government Work Plan (RKPD), and Regional Work Unit Work Plan and Budget (RKA SKPD).
6. The integration of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women is facilitated by the work unit whose duties and functions handle the empowerment of women in the region in coordination with the Regional Development Planning Agency.

Article 7

Women victims of violence have the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, both Government and Non-Government.

CHAPTER IV

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 6

(1) Women have the right to obtain special protection from things that threaten their safety and/or health.

(2) Special protection is given to women because their reproductive function is guaranteed and protected by law.

Article 3

The objectives of Protection and Empowerment of Women are to: a. prevent and address risks from the vulnerability of women so that their survival can be fulfilled in accordance with minimum basic needs;
b. empower women both individually and in groups, and communities experiencing gender issues so that they are able to meet their needs independently; and
c. increase the participation of women both individually and in groups as potential and resources in the implementation of social community life.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women in the history of human life have indeed been in a disadvantageous condition. This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a deplorable condition.

In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it still needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.

In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

CHAPTER VII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 21

(1) To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine developments in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women in the region.

(3) Monitoring shall be carried out periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Work Units that implement policies, programs and activities for the protection of women.

(4) Monitoring shall be carried out from the planning stage to the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women for the current year.

Article 14

1. The implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women in the region is carried out by establishing, developing, strengthening, or utilizing task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions.

(2) The membership of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of relevant Regional Work Units, Community Institutions, Universities, and civil society.

3. The establishment of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent Decree.

CHAPTER X

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 25

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, all provisions relating to the protection and empowerment of women insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation shall remain in force.

Article 22

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women shall be carried out at the end of each fiscal year.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women for the following year.

(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 11

(1) The Regional Government provides protection and comfort and seeks to fulfill basic needs for women who are in conflict areas and/or disaster-affected areas.

(2) The forms of protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER II

PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2

Protection and Empowerment of Women is based on: a. respect for Human Rights;
b. justice and gender equality;
c. non-discrimination; and
d. protection.

PROVINCE OF SOUTH KALIMANTAN

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TAPIN REGENCY

NUMBER 02 YEAR 2015

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

CHAPTER VI

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 20

(1) The community may participate in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. cooperation;
b. active role in policy formulation; and
c. complaints/reports.

(4) The procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 15

1. In implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women, the Regional Government may cooperate with International Institutions.
(2) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of statutory regulations.

CHAPTER VIII

FUNDING

Article 23

(1) Funding for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women in the region shall be sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, and other lawful sources of income that are not binding.

(2) In the event that the region receives funding assistance for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women from the Government, it shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

CHAPTER IX

REPORTING

Article 24

(1) The Regent shall submit a report on the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women in the region to the Governor.

(2) The implementation of reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out annually and/or when necessary. (3) The form of reporting as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER V

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

Article 18

(1) In order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family life, society, nation, and state, women must be empowered.

(2) Women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is directed towards obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings, and being able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Article 19

(1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility in efforts to empower women.

(2) Women's empowerment efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women in the history of human life have indeed been in a disadvantageous condition. This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a deplorable condition.

In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it still needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.

In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 21

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine developments in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women in the region.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women in the history of human life have indeed been in a disadvantageous condition. This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a deplorable condition.

In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it still needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.

In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

CHAPTER IV

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 13

(1) The Regent implements policies, programs and activities for the protection of women, to eliminate all forms of discrimination and violence against women in the region.

(2) The implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be coordinated by the Vice Regent.

(3) The work unit whose duties and functions handle the empowerment of women implements policies, programs and activities for the protection of women that have been established, and in its implementation cooperates with Regional Work Units, Community Institutions, Universities, and civil society.

(4) The implementation as referred to in paragraph (3) is in the form of: policy analysis, coordination, advocacy, socialization, communication, information, and education (KIE), training, service facilitation, service provision, model development, and other forms.

5. The integration of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women into regional development planning, which is set forth in planning and budget documents covering the Regional Long-Term Development Plan (RPJPD), Regional Medium-Term Plan (RPJMD), Regional Work Unit Strategic Plan (Renstra SKPD), Regional Government Work Plan (RKPD), and Regional Work Unit Work Plan and Budget (RKA SKPD).
6. The integration of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women is facilitated by the work unit whose duties and functions handle the empowerment of women in the region in coordination with the Regional Development Planning Agency.

Article 14

1. The implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women in the region is carried out by establishing, developing, strengthening, or utilizing task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions.

(2) The membership of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of relevant Regional Work Units, Community Institutions, Universities, and civil society.

3. The establishment of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent Decree.

Article 15

1. In implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women, the Regional Government may cooperate with International Institutions.
(2) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of statutory regulations.

Article 12

The Regional Government facilitates the establishment of women's protection institutions.

Article 7

Women victims of violence have the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, both Government and Non-Government.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine developments in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women in the region.

(3) Monitoring shall be carried out periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Work Units that implement policies, programs and activities for the protection of women.

(4) Monitoring shall be carried out from the planning stage to the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women for the current year.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tapin Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of the Regional Government of Tapin Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tapin.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Tapin Regency.
5. Agency is the Agency for Women's Empowerment and Family Planning of Tapin Regency.
6. Head of Agency is the Head of the Agency for Women's Empowerment and Family Planning of Tapin Regency.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that have equality in accordance with the development and socio-cultural conditions of society.
8. Gender-Based Violence is any act of deviation caused by an imbalance in the relationship between women and men that results in misery or suffering of women including children, whether physically, sexually and/or psychologically, including threats, certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily that occurs in the private/domestic sphere and in the public sphere.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.
10. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capabilities so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.

ll.Disability is a permanent physical, mental and intellectual, or sensory impairment.

THE REGENT OF TAPIN,

Considering:
a. that women as a national asset who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination; b. that in addition to protection as referred to in letter a, women need to be empowered so that they can actualize their potential optimally to participate in development; c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letters a and b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Protection and Empowerment of Women; In view of: 1. Article 3

The objectives of Protection and Empowerment of Women are to: a. prevent and address risks from the vulnerability of women so that their survival can be fulfilled in accordance with minimum basic needs;
b. empower women both individually and in groups, and communities experiencing gender issues so that they are able to meet their needs independently; and
c. increase the participation of women both individually and in groups as potential and resources in the implementation of social community life.

Article 22

(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women shall be carried out at the end of each fiscal year.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women for the following year.

(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VIII

FUNDING

Article 23

(1) Funding for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women in the region shall be sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, and other lawful sources of income that are not binding.

(2) In the event that the region receives funding assistance for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women from the Government, it shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

a. cooperation;
b. active role in policy formulation; and
c. complaints/reports.

(4) The procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women in the history of human life have indeed been in a disadvantageous condition. This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a deplorable condition.

In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it still needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.

In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

a. cooperation;
b. active role in policy formulation; and
c. complaints/reports.

(4) The procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women in the history of human life have indeed been in a disadvantageous condition. This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a deplorable condition.

In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it still needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.

In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

b. empower women both individually and in groups, and communities experiencing gender issues so that they are able to meet their needs independently; and
c. increase the participation of women both individually and in groups as potential and resources in the implementation of social community life.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women in the history of human life have indeed been in a disadvantageous condition. This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a deplorable condition.

In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it still needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.

In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

CHAPTER V

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

Article 18

(1) In order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family life, society, nation, and state, women must be empowered.

(2) Women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is directed towards obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings, and being able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Article 7

Women victims of violence have the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions, both Government and Non-Government.

Article 3

The objectives of Protection and Empowerment of Women are to: a. prevent and address risks from the vulnerability of women so that their survival can be fulfilled in accordance with minimum basic needs;
b. empower women both individually and in groups, and communities experiencing gender issues so that they are able to meet their needs independently; and
c. increase the participation of women both individually and in groups as potential and resources in the implementation of social community life.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women in the history of human life have indeed been in a disadvantageous condition. This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a deplorable condition.

In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it still needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.

In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

(2) Women's empowerment efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women in the history of human life have indeed been in a disadvantageous condition. This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a deplorable condition.

In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it still needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.

In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a deplorable condition.

In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it still needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.

In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

CHAPTER IV

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 6

(1) Women have the right to obtain special protection from things that threaten their safety and/or health.

(2) Special protection is given to women because their reproductive function is guaranteed and protected by law.

CHAPTER VIII

FUNDING

Article 23

(1) Funding for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women in the region shall be sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, and other lawful sources of income that are not binding.

(2) In the event that the region receives funding assistance for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women from the Government, it shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 14

1. The implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women in the region is carried out by establishing, developing, strengthening, or utilizing task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions.

(2) The membership of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of relevant Regional Work Units, Community Institutions, Universities, and civil society.

3. The establishment of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent Decree.

CHAPTER IX

REPORTING

Article 24

(1) The Regent shall submit a report on the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women in the region to the Governor.

(2) The implementation of reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out annually and/or when necessary. (3) The form of reporting as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 15

1. In implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women, the Regional Government may cooperate with International Institutions.
(2) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of statutory regulations.

CHAPTER VII

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 21

(1) To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women, the Regional Government shall conduct monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine developments in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women in the region.

(3) Monitoring shall be carried out periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Work Units that implement policies, programs and activities for the protection of women.

(4) Monitoring shall be carried out from the planning stage to the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women for the current year.

Article 3

The objectives of Protection and Empowerment of Women are to: a. prevent and address risks from the vulnerability of women so that their survival can be fulfilled in accordance with minimum basic needs;
b. empower women both individually and in groups, and communities experiencing gender issues so that they are able to meet their needs independently; and
c. increase the participation of women both individually and in groups as potential and resources in the implementation of social community life.

Article 19

(1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility in efforts to empower women.

(2) Women's empowerment efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VI

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 20

(1) The community may participate in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations.

(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. cooperation;
b. active role in policy formulation; and
c. complaints/reports.

(4) The procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 3

The objectives of Protection and Empowerment of Women are to: a. prevent and address risks from the vulnerability of women so that their survival can be fulfilled in accordance with minimum basic needs;

c. increase the participation of women both individually and in groups as potential and resources in the implementation of social community life.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women in the history of human life have indeed been in a disadvantageous condition. This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a deplorable condition.

In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it still needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.

In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Gender-Based Violence is any act of deviation caused by an imbalance in the relationship between women and men that results in misery or suffering of women including children, whether physically, sexually and/or psychologically, including threats, certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily that occurs in the private/domestic sphere and in the public sphere.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women in the history of human life have indeed been in a disadvantageous condition. This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a deplorable condition.

In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it still needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.

In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Article 3

The objectives of Protection and Empowerment of Women are to: a. prevent and address risks from the vulnerability of women so that their survival can be fulfilled in accordance with minimum basic needs;
b. empower women both individually and in groups, and communities experiencing gender issues so that they are able to meet their needs independently; and
c. increase the participation of women both individually and in groups as potential and resources in the implementation of social community life.

Article 12

Article 13

(1) The Regent implements policies, programs and activities for the protection of women, to eliminate all forms of discrimination and violence against women in the region.

(2) The implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be coordinated by the Vice Regent.

(3) The work unit whose duties and functions handle the empowerment of women implements policies, programs and activities for the protection of women that have been established, and in its implementation cooperates with Regional Work Units, Community Institutions, Universities, and civil society.

(4) The implementation as referred to in paragraph (3) is in the form of: policy analysis, coordination, advocacy, socialization, communication, information, and education (KIE), training, service facilitation, service provision, model development, and other forms.

5. The integration of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women into regional development planning, which is set forth in planning and budget documents covering the Regional Long-Term Development Plan (RPJPD), Regional Medium-Term Plan (RPJMD), Regional Work Unit Strategic Plan (Renstra SKPD), Regional Government Work Plan (RKPD), and Regional Work Unit Work Plan and Budget (RKA SKPD).
6. The integration of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women is facilitated by the work unit whose duties and functions handle the empowerment of women in the region in coordination with the Regional Development Planning Agency.

Article 9

(1) Companies that employ female workers are required to provide protection in accordance with applicable statutory regulations.

(2) The protection that must be provided by companies to women as workers as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

(2) The membership of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of relevant Regional Work Units, Community Institutions, Universities, and civil society.

3. The establishment of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent Decree.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tapin Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of the Regional Government of Tapin Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tapin.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Tapin Regency.
5. Agency is the Agency for Women's Empowerment and Family Planning of Tapin Regency.
6. Head of Agency is the Head of the Agency for Women's Empowerment and Family Planning of Tapin Regency.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that have equality in accordance with the development and socio-cultural conditions of society.
8. Gender-Based Violence is any act of deviation caused by an imbalance in the relationship between women and men that results in misery or suffering of women including children, whether physically, sexually and/or psychologically, including threats, certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily that occurs in the private/domestic sphere and in the public sphere.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.
10. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capabilities so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.

ll.Disability is a permanent physical, mental and intellectual, or sensory impairment.

Article 15

(2) Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of statutory regulations.

(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women in the history of human life have indeed been in a disadvantageous condition. This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a deplorable condition.

In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it still needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.

In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women in the history of human life have indeed been in a disadvantageous condition. This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a deplorable condition.

In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it still needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.

In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women in the history of human life have indeed been in a disadvantageous condition. This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a deplorable condition.

In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it still needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.

In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

REGENT OF TAPIN

PROVINCE OF SOUTH KALIMANTAN

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TAPIN REGENCY

NUMBER 02 YEAR 2015

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

CONCERNING

PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women in the history of human life have indeed been in a disadvantageous condition. This means that in social community life, women have always been the party that is placed second after men, and even more tragically, the history of women in their social life can be said to have experienced a deplorable condition.

In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it still needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as national assets who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.

In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, namely a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, national defense and security activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Tapin Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the organizer of the Regional Government of Tapin Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tapin.
4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Tapin Regency.
5. Agency is the Agency for Women's Empowerment and Family Planning of Tapin Regency.
6. Head of Agency is the Head of the Agency for Women's Empowerment and Family Planning of Tapin Regency.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that have equality in accordance with the development and socio-cultural conditions of society.
8. Gender-Based Violence is any act of deviation caused by an imbalance in the relationship between women and men that results in misery or suffering of women including children, whether physically, sexually and/or psychologically, including threats, certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily that occurs in the private/domestic sphere and in the public sphere.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.
10. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capabilities so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.

ll.Disability is a permanent physical, mental and intellectual, or sensory impairment.

Article 19

(1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility in efforts to empower women.

(2) Women's empowerment efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

a. cooperation;
b. active role in policy formulation; and

(4) The procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.
